He opposes the death penalty and has supported clemency reforms allowing commutation of harsh sentences imposed under now-repealed mandatory minimum provisions.
rows.name: Edward Markey

rows.reasoning: McGovern consistently favors diversion over prosecution: he supported drug courts, opposed mandatory minimum sentences for drug offenses, and backed decriminalization of marijuana possession. He has consistently voted to reduce incarceration for non-violent offenses and shift prosecutorial resources away from low-level drug crimes toward violent crime.
rows.name: Jim McGovern

rows.reasoning: Mitchell's entire criminal justice platform is built around diversion over prosecution: Care First Jails Last, the Care First Pretrial Agency, jail-based diversion expansion, juvenile hall depopulation, and the county's Violence Prevention strategy in parks. As a state senator she authored SB 190 to eliminate fees that trapped juveniles in the system. She has consistently prioritized treatment, rehabilitation, and community-based alternatives over prosecution.
rows.name: Holly J. Mitchell

rows.reasoning: Moulton supports legalizing marijuana and reducing drug-based convictions, and backs diversion programs over incarceration for non-violent offenses. His criminal justice philosophy consistently prioritizes alternatives to prosecution and rehabilitation for non-violent cases.
rows.name: Seth Moulton

rows.name: Adrin Nazarian

rows.reasoning: Neal's criminal justice record favors deprioritizing prosecution of non-violent drug offenses — he voted to reduce marijuana sentencing disparities and supported sentencing reform that shifted enforcement resources toward violent crime. rows.name: Richard Neal

rows.reasoning: Pressley has consistently supported progressive prosecutorial approaches — declining to prosecute low-level offenses, diversion for drug possession, and focusing resources on violent crime. She has backed reform prosecutors in Boston and nationally. She introduced the People's Justice Guarantee which would direct prosecutorial resources toward serious crimes while decriminalizing many nonviolent offenses. She has explicitly endorsed the "harm reduction" prosecutorial philosophy.
rows.name: Ayanna Pressley

rows.name: William Smith
